question: Is full covariance preconditioning a material cost in this small real-text training setup on this Mac?
scope: Necessary cost screen only; not candidate performance or time-to-target-loss evaluation
data: 96 January2025 research abstracts selected deterministically from the local corpus; byte tokens; next32 documents reserved unused
device: MPS, with general CPU fallback disabled; record internal fallback warnings

covariance.contract: four input blocks, each width d
covariance.first_refresh: step32, with identity inverse before first refresh

muon.qkv: split packed gradient into three square blocks for NS
muon.scale: sqrt(max(rows,cols)) per matrix; sqrt(d) for each QKV block

timing: Synchronize at end-to-end window boundaries only. Separate instrumented runs synchronize components; do not equate their sums with uninstrumented timings.
matched_controls: Same byte batches, initialization and schedule per width/arm; all non-Muon parameters use AdamW
gate: A measured preconditioning cost fraction above5% of total instrumented training step supports only further profiling. If below5% stop this configuration. End-to-end matched-arm difference and synchronization distortion must also be reported.
still_required: source polynomial inverse and larger refresh interval controls
iterative low-rank refresh and apply cost
full NewtonMuon must beat Muon in time-to-loss before approximating it
limitations: No candidate low-rank path in this first screen
Not exact author-code or optimized CUDA-kernel reproduction
No held-out loss or novelty claim
Warmup is compilation/runtime warmup, not convergence
dtype: float32 throughout, including NS; differs from source BF16 NS implementation
source_audit_amendment: Before any profiling run: verified refresh-only covariance, identity initial inverse, QKV split NS and scale against pinned author code. Retain first draft freeze separately.
